name: TouchDesigner
description: Opens TouchDesigner projects and forwards commands to a Web Server DAT inside them. Aperture is only the wire — what a command means is decided by your .toe file, not by this app.

actions.name: process.launch
actions.description: Open one of the TouchDesigner projects configured on this machine. Names a project set up in Aperture's settings, not a file path. It takes several seconds to come up, so anything sent straight afterwards may find nothing listening yet — wait_for it before the next step rather than trying and retrying.

project.description: Which configured project to open. Omit to use the default.

actions.name: process.close
actions.description: Ask TouchDesigner to close. Nothing is force-closed, so a project with unsaved work can refuse and put a save dialog on that machine's own screen.

actions.name: switch_scene
actions.description: Switch the running TouchDesigner project to one of its scenes. Only the names the project itself reports are real; if none are listed, or one is rejected, call list_scenes rather than guessing — the list can be out of date.

scene.description: Scene name, exactly as the project reports it.

actions.name: list_scenes
actions.description: Ask the running TouchDesigner project which scenes it has, and remember the answer. Worth calling when the listed scenes look stale or empty, or after one was rejected.

actions.name: send_command
actions.description: Send any other command the TouchDesigner project implements. Aperture does not know what commands exist — the project decides, and an unknown one comes back as an error rather than silently doing nothing.

args.description: Arguments for it. Omit when it takes none.
